title: tier-2 shipped code: the MRNM offset-to-pointer rebase against MrnmFixup (0x141b893e0)
notes: SHIPPED-CODE tier-2 unit. The candidate is crates/ow-tank/src/mrnm.rs (fixup), built by cargo and called by crates/ow-tank/src/bin/verify_probe.rs through the mrnm_fixup entry. The ledger binds the verdict to mrnm.rs + the probe source + the git revision.

Oracle is MrnmFixup at exe 0x141b893e0 (v2b 0x7ff7c68a93e0), 0xEB bytes. It rebases three header qwords, then per vertex buffer the element-array slot (+0x10) and, only when flags bit 0x10 is clear, the two data-stream slots (+0x50/+0x58), then per index buffer the data slot (+0x08). A stored zero stays zero; the submesh descriptors are not touched.

The payload keeps every slot in its file-relative form; the client's dead second argument (RDX) carries the payload's arena base on both sides, so the oracle and the probe write the same absolute pointer values and the whole 0x700-byte payload is compared without masking any slot.

The fixture varies the two loop counts (0..3 each), the 0x10 flag per vertex buffer, an element count of zero, and puts non-zero data in the submesh index-start block at +0x40..+0x60 so a spurious write there is caught.
The function has no allocator or external call; every branch is reachable, so coverage is measured across all of them.
acknowledgedGaps: Offset arithmetic only: the unit proves the rebase formula and the exact slot set. It says nothing about what the pointers point at; that is fn/MrnmHandler.
The client has no bounds check. The 0x700-byte payload keeps every rebased address inside it; a stored offset that would leave the payload is not generated.
